latin: Si duplex Aleph quod est in textu: Non auferetur sceptrum, etc., coniunxerimus ad duplex Aleph quod est in textu: Deus possedit me ab initio, et ad duplex Aleph quod est in textu: Terra autem erat inanis, per uiam Cabalae intelligemus ibi Iacob de illo uero Messia locutum, qui fuit Iesus Nazarenus.
translation: If we join the double alef in the text The scepter shall not be taken away, etc., to the double alef in the text God possessed me from the beginning, and to the double alef in the text But the earth was without form, by way of the Cabala we shall understand that there Jacob was speaking of that true Messiah, who was Jesus of Nazareth.
translation_note: The three texts joined are Gen. 49:10 (spoken by Jacob), Prov. 8:22, and Gen. 1:2 (farmer1998:27102); each alef functions as a linking mark across otherwise unconnected verses rather than as an argued proof.
